instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1203 Minimum wage; youth minimum wage; adjustments (as amended by Laws 2026, LB258, eff. 2026-07-18)
figure_or_rule_carried: (1)(e) 15.00/h 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31; (2) from 2027-01-01 and each 1 January: +1.75% (fixed step, LB258 2026 replaced the CPI indexing of Initiative 433); NDOL publishes next rate by 15 October from 2026-10-15; (3) tipped cash wage 2.13/h, wages + tips >= minimum, burden on employer; (4) student-learners >= 75% of the applicable minimum; (5) youth minimum wage 13.50/h for age 14-15 not emancipated, +1.5% every fifth year from 2030-01-01 rounded to the cent. Derived 2027 adult rate 15.00 x 1.0175 = 15.2625 (statute states no rounding rule for the adult rate)
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 20260827231606 of nebraskalegislature.gov); 2027 value derived arithmetically

figure_or_rule_carried: New employee under 20 (not seasonal/migrant): training wage >= 75% of the FEDERAL minimum wage for 90 days from hire; +90 days during Commissioner-approved OJT; max one-fourth of total hours paid at training rate; no displacement
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 20260113080850; not re-checked after LB258)

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1202 Wage and Hour Act definitions (coverage)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 4 or more employees at any one time (excl. seasonal employment of 20 weeks or less); excludes US, State and political subdivisions. Employee excludes agriculture, baby-sitters in private homes, bona fide executive/administrative/professional, government, volunteers, apprentices/learners, VA trainees, child employed by parent and vice versa, rehabilitation programme workers

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1229 Wage Payment and Collection Act definitions (wages, fringe benefits, payroll debit card)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages include fringe benefits when agreed and conditions met; paid leave other than earned but unused VACATION is not due at separation unless agreed, i.e. earned unused vacation is wages payable at separation; ABC test for employee status under the Act; payroll debit card defined

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1230.01 Unpaid commissions at separation
figure_or_rule_carried: At separation, commissions due on the next regular payday after the employer receives customer payment; periodic accounting of outstanding commissions until paid

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1230(1),(3),(4) paydays, deductions, payroll debit card, final pay
figure_or_rule_carried: (1) wages on regular paydays designated or agreed; 30 days written notice before paydays are altered; deductions only if required/permitted by law, court order, or written agreement. (3) payroll debit card: 15 U.S.C. 1693k compulsory-use rule; at least one free withdrawal per pay period (not more than once a week) up to net wages; no card fees to employee. (4)(a) separation (non-political-subdivision): unpaid wages due next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner; (b) political subdivisions: within two weeks of the next governing-body meeting. No statutory minimum pay frequency
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 20261013091117, file already held)

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-3803 and 48-3804 Healthy Families and Workplaces Act (paid sick time accrual, carryover, use)
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrual starts after 80 hours of consecutive employment, 1 hour per 30 hours worked; earn/use cap per year 40 h (small business) or 56 h (other) unless employer sets higher; exempt employees assumed 40 h/week; front-load allowed; carryover required (use cap still applies) or pay-out-and-front-load alternative; PTO policy meeting the minimum satisfies; reinstatement on rehire within 12 months; NO payout at separation required (48-3803(10)); documentation after 3 consecutive work days; use in hourly or smallest payroll increment

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-3802 Healthy Families and Workplaces Act definitions (Initiative Law 2024 No. 436 text) incl. paid sick time pay rate
figure_or_rule_carried: Pre-LB415 text (snapshot 2025-03-11). Carried for 48-3802(7) only, which LB415 did not amend in the slip-law text read: paid sick time paid at the same hourly rate and with the same benefits as hours worked, never below the 48-1203 minimum. Coverage and small-business definitions superseded by LB415 (US-NES5-009)

instrument_name: Laws 2025, LB415 (slip law, approved 2025-06-04) amending Initiative Law 2024 No. 436 sec. 2-4, 8 and Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-665
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = employs 11 or more employees (was 1); small business = at least 11 but fewer than 20 employees in a given week (not if 20+ in each of 20+ weeks of current or preceding year); employee excludes owner-operators, independent contractors, under 80 hours in NE per calendar year, seasonal/temporary agricultural employment, RUIA railroad employees, individuals under 16; State and political subdivisions excluded

instrument_name: 2026 Nebraska Circular EN (Rev. 11-2025): percentage-method tables, filing calendar, deposits, special withholding, nonresident personal services
figure_or_rule_carried: Percentage method 2026 annual single: 0 to 3,430 nil; 2.26% over 3,430; 74.13 + 3.22% over 6,710; 560.35 + 4.21% over 21,810; 972.93 + 4.35% over 31,610; 1,343.55 + 4.48% over 40,130; 2,922.30 + 4.60% over 75,370. Annual married: nil to 8,190; 2.26% over 8,190; 108.93 + 3.22% over 13,010; 733.29 + 4.21% over 32,400; 1,491.09 + 4.35% over 50,400; 2,018.75 + 4.48% over 62,530; 2,932.22 + 4.60% over 82,920 (subtract allowances first, 2,440 each). Employers with more than 24 employees must withhold at least 1.5% of taxable wages unless documented. W-4N exemption must be renewed by 15 February each year; W-4 after 2019 without W-4N = single, zero allowances. Deposits: Form 501N/EFT by the 15th of the following month when more than 500 withheld in month 1 or month 2 of a quarter; Form 941N quarterly by last day of month after quarter (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); annual filers one 941N by 31 January; W-3N + state W-2/1099 copies by 31 January; EFT mandatory if prior-year payments exceeded 5,000; more than 50 W-2/1099 must be e-filed. Nonresident personal services (not employees, not subject to federal withholding): 4% of net payment under 28,000, 6% at 28,000 or more (W-4NA/W-4NB); unregistered construction contractor 5%. Employer must hold a Nebraska withholding licence

instrument_name: NDOL Employer's Guide to Unemployment Insurance (Revised 9/11/2025): registration, wage reports, deadlines, multistate, wage-base credit
figure_or_rule_carried: UI Form 1 registration (Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-612) via NEworks; quarterly Combined Tax Report + Wage Report due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31 (delinquent after last day of month after quarter; interest 1.5%/month; late-report penalty 0.1% of gross wages, min 25, max 200 after 10th day of second month); wage report items: SSN, last name + first and middle initials, quarter gross wages; optional hours paid and primary job title; NEworks online or FTP file (specs at dol.nebraska.gov/UITax); e-file expected if payroll exceeded 100,000 in either of two prior years (48-648); combined tax employer-paid, not withheld (48-648(1)); wage base 9,000 (cat 1-19) / 24,000 (cat 20); wages paid for services in another state or by a predecessor count toward the base (48-648.02); SUIT portion 0-20% of combined tax (48-649.01(3)); localization: all service in NE, or base of operations, direction/control, residence tests (48-604(2)); domestic employers covered at 1,000 cash wages in a quarter, agricultural at 10 workers in 20 weeks or 20,000 in a quarter (48-604(4)); separation information via SIDES within 10 days

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-1558 Wages subject to garnishment
figure_or_rule_carried: Weekly garnishment max = lesser of 25% of disposable earnings, disposable earnings above 30 x federal minimum hourly wage, or 15% if the debtor is head of a family; limits do not apply to support orders, Chapter 13 orders, state/federal tax debts; no discharge for one garnishment; other pay periods use Commissioner multiples
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 20250314043147; last amended 2001)

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-237 Employer; prohibited use of social security numbers
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer shall not publicly post/display more than the last four SSN digits (incl. making them available to coworkers), require transmission of more than the last four over the Internet unless secure/encrypted, require more than the last four to access a website without password/PIN, or use more than the last four as an employee number; full SSN allowed for legal compliance and internal administrative purposes (benefits, screening, staffing)

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-2303 New-hire reporting to DHHS
figure_or_rule_carried: Every hire or rehire reported to DHHS: employee name, address, SSN, date of hire/rehire; employer name, address, FEIN; copy of federal W-4 with hire date or approved form; mail, fax, electronic; within 20 days of hire/rehire, or two monthly electronic transmissions 12-16 days apart. NDOL guide gives the Nebraska State Directory of New Hires, PO Box 144013 Austin TX, newhire-reporting.com

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 43-1725 and 43-1726 Income Withholding for Child Support Act (employer duties)
figure_or_rule_carried: No discrimination/discipline/termination for income withholding (civil fine up to 500 per violation, restitution); notice to withhold terminates for the employer 30 days after the obligor leaves; employer returns a copy of the notice indicating cessation with forwarding information. Employer fee and priority sections (43-1720 to 43-1724) NOT read

instrument_name: Nebraska DOR Electronic and Media Reporting of W-2 and 1099 page; Important Information on Preparing Federal Forms W-2 (box 15)
figure_or_rule_carried: Resources: NebFile online W-2/1099 filing; Nebraska Computer Reporting Procedure 21CM (11/2025) and 21EFW2 (11/2025). W-2 box 15: 'NE' then the employer Nebraska ID number (4 to 8 digits) exactly as on Forms 941N/W-3N

instrument_name: Nebraska Computer Reporting Procedure, 21EFW2 (Information Guide 8-633, November 2025)
article_or_section: Overview; Code RS and RV record layouts
figure_or_rule_carried: W-3N and all W-2/1099/W-2G with NE income/withholding due 31 January (next business day if weekend/holiday); more than 50 forms must be e-filed via NebFile for Business; magnetic media not processed; file in SSA EFW2 format with Nebraska RS record (state code 31, taxing entity code '31') and RV state total record (count of RS31 records, total state income tax withheld); bulk filers request ID/PIN from DOR

instrument_name: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2715.03 Individual income tax brackets and rates (as amended by Laws 2023, LB754)
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory rates: brackets 1-2 at 2.46% and 3.51%; rate three 4.55% for tax years 2026, 3.99% from 2027; rate four 5.20% for 2025, 4.55% for 2026, 3.99% from 2027. Bracket amounts CPI-U indexed annually (12 months to 31 Aug of the prior year vs 2016 base), rounded to nearest 10 (5 rounds up), schedules prescribed by the Tax Commissioner. Assessment-level schedule; withholding uses the DOR Circular EN tables (2026 withholding rates 2.26%-4.60%, US-NES5-010), which are DOR-designed and differ from the statutory rates

instrument_name: NDOL Employer's Guide to Unemployment Insurance (Revised 9/11/2025): excluded services under Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-604 and reportable wages
figure_or_rule_carried: UI-excluded services (48-604): casual labour under 50 a quarter; family employment (child under 21 employed by parent, spouse, parent employed by child) in sole proprietorships/partnerships; church and religious-order service and ministers; students employed by their school and spouses; student nurses/interns; commission-only real-estate/insurance agents; newspaper delivery under 18; elected officials, national guard etc.; inmates; owner-operator truck drivers; direct sellers; AmeriCorps; election workers under 1,000/year; academic-credit work by full-time students at nonprofit/public schools. Reportable: tips reported to employer, sick pay, 401(k) deferrals, corporate officers' pay, board/lodging at Commissioner values (NAC 220 ch. 2)
